notes:
Here are the verse-by-verse notes based on the sources retrieved. The commentary tradition for these genealogical and liturgical chapters is largely shared across Protestant traditions; where I could not find distinct tradition-specific differences, I note the traditional consensus.

---

## Overview of the Passage

Ellicott notes that 1 Chronicles 6 contains three large sections: (1) the Aaronite high-priestly line through Eleazar to the exile (vv. 1–15); (2) a double series of the sons of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, leading to the ancestry of Heman, Asaph, and Ethan — David's three choir-masters (vv. 16–48); and (3) a repetition of the Aaronite line as a prelude to the list of Levitical cities (vv. 49–81). Our passage (vv. 28–54) bridges the genealogical fragments into the temple musicians and priestly ministries, then transitions to the territorial allotments.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

---

## Verse-by-Verse Notes

### v. 28 — "The sons of Samuel: Joel his firstborn and Abijah his second son."

**Traditional reading:** The BSB (and KJV-based translations) correctly name Joel as Samuel's firstborn and Abijah (Abiah) as his second. Ellicott notes that in the KJV the Hebrew text had a corruption: "Vashni" is not a proper name but a mangled form of the Hebrew phrase *w'sheni* ("and the second"). The name "Joel" had dropped out, so the KJV reads "the firstborn Vashni, and Abiah." The correct reading — confirmed by 1 Samuel 8:2 and v. 33 below — is "Joel the firstborn, and the second Abiah."

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Gill** agrees: Vashni is a corruption; the Syriac and Arabic versions read "Joel" here, matching 1 Chronicles 6:33. Joel = Vashni/Joel; Abiah = Abijah.

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Coke's Commentary** adds that the end of v. 27 should read "Samuel his son" to make the link explicit from Elkanah to Samuel, as Houbigant suggested.

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tcc/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### vv. 29–30 — "The descendants of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son, Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, and Asaiah his son."

**Traditional reading:** This traces the line of Mahli (one of Merari's two sons, the other being Mushi) through seven generations to Asaiah. Gill notes the line of Mushi is omitted here (it appears in vv. 44–47 for Ethan the Merarite singer). Ellicott adds that all these names are otherwise unknown; they are "genuine relics of ancient family registers" preserved by the Chronicler for their antiquarian as well as legal value in the post-exilic community.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm
— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

---

### v. 31 — "These are the men David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there."

**Traditional reading:** "These" refers forward to Heman, Asaph, and Ethan (vv. 33–47). Ellicott explains the phrase "set over the service of song" (literally, "made stand by the hands of song") as appointing them to minister to the sacred music — to manage and conduct it. The timing is "after the ark had rest," meaning after David brought the Ark to Jerusalem and placed it in the tent he pitched on Mount Zion (2 Samuel 6:17). Before that, the Ark had been moved from place to place and even captured by the Philistines.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm
— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Keil & Delitzsch** render it: "from the resting of the ark," i.e., from the time the Ark received a permanent resting-place on Zion and became the centre of the worship instituted by David.

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### v. 32 — "They ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. And they performed their duties according to the regulations given them."

**Traditional reading:** The "dwelling of the Tent of Meeting" refers to the tent David erected on Zion to house the Ark. Ellicott notes that this Davidic tent is called by the old Mosaic name *'ōhel mō'ēd* ("tent of meeting"). The ancient Mosaic tabernacle still stood at Gibeon (1 Chronicles 21:29; 2 Chronicles 1:3), but the Ark was in David's tent on Zion. The singers ministered there until Solomon's Temple replaced both.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

Gill: "they waited on their office according to their order" — David prescribed the manner and order of service (cf. 1 Chronicles 25:1).

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Lange's Commentary** adds: "In their order" (*k'mishpatam*) means according to the arrangement prescribed by David, namely that Heman stood in the centre, Asaph on his right, and Ethan on his left (see vv. 33, 39, 44).

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/lcc/1-chronicles-6.html

**Coke's Commentary** (homiletical reflection): "The work of praise in the great congregation should be as much the minister's care, as the work of prayer. It is a sure sign of a decay of godliness, when there is a neglect of divine psalmody."

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tcc/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### v. 33 — "These are the men who served, together with their sons. From the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel."

**Traditional reading:** After the parenthetic v. 32, the main sentence from v. 31 is resumed. "These" are Heman, Asaph, and Ethan; their "sons" are the members of their musical guilds (Ellicott compares the phrase "sons of the prophets" — 2 Kings 9:1). Ellicott also notes that Heman is called "the singer" (*ham'shōrēr*), meaning a minstrel who both sings and plays an instrument. That Heman is grandson of Samuel the prophet is "an undesigned coincidence" confirming Samuel's Levitical ancestry (which some have questioned because 1 Samuel presents Elkanah as an Ephraimite).

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

Gill: "Heman a singer; the chief of the singers, and who composed psalms and hymns, which are in the book of Psalms."

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Guzik overview:** Heman is a Kohathite; his descendants will compose many psalms and teach Israel to sing truth.

— https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm (Guzik commentary section)

---

### vv. 34–38 — Heman's genealogy traced from Joel back through Samuel, Elkanah, Jeroham, Eliel, Toah, Zuph, Elkanah, Mahath, Amasai, Elkanah, Joel, Azariah, Zephaniah, Tahath, Assir, Ebiasaph, Korah, Izhar, Kohath, Levi, to Israel (Jacob).

**Traditional reading:** This is the "continuous list" that helps untangle the fragmentary genealogy of vv. 22–28. Ellicott traces the correspondences: Toah = Nahath (v. 26); Zuph = Zophai (v. 26); Eliel = Eliab (v. 27); Mahath = Ahimoth (v. 25); the three Elkanahs, Amasai, Joel, Azariah, Zephaniah, Tahath, Assir, Ebiasaph, and Korah correspond to the fragmentary list with variant names.

Special note: Heman descends from **Korah** (v. 37), the same Korah who led the rebellion against Moses (Numbers 16). Yet his descendants became temple singers — the "sons of Korah" who authored several Psalms (Psalms 42, 44–49, 84–85, 87–88). This is often noted as an example of grace: the line that once rebelled became the line that led worship.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

Gill: the genealogy runs through Izhar → Kohath → Levi → Israel, tracing Heman's Levitical credentials to the patriarch.

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

---

### vv. 39–43 — Asaph's genealogy: son of Berechiah, traced back through Shimea, Michael, Baaseiah, Malchijah, Ethni, Zerah, Adaiah, Ethan, Zimmah, Shimei, Jahath, Gershom, to Levi.

**Traditional reading:** Asaph is called Heman's "brother" (v. 39) — meaning kinsman or fellow-craftsman, not literal brother. He is a Gershonite (descended from Gershom/Gershon, Levi's eldest son). He "stood on his right hand," meaning his choir was positioned to Heman's right. Asaph is well-known from the Psalter: twelve Psalms bear his name (Psalm 50, 73–83).

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm
— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Keil & Delitzsch** note that Asaph's genealogy has only fifteen names back to Gershon, compared to Heman's twenty to Kohath — likely because intermediate links are omitted in places.

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### vv. 44–47 — Ethan's (Jeduthun's) genealogy: son of Kishi, traced back through Abdi, Malluch, Hashabiah, Amaziah, Hilkiah, Amzi, Bani, Shemer, Mahli, Mushi, Merari, to Levi.

**Traditional reading:** Ethan is a Merarite, descended through Mushi (Mahli's brother). His choir stood on Heman's left. Gill notes Ethan is also called Jeduthun (1 Chronicles 16:41; 25:1; Psalms 39, 62, 77 titles). Keil & Delitzsch explain that *Yeduthun* ("praiseman") was probably a by-name he received from his calling.

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm
— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/1-chronicles-6.html

**Dummelow** confirms: the names Heman, Asaph, and Ethan (Jeduthun) are familiar from Psalm titles.

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcb/1-chronicles-6.html

**Guzik overview:** David appoints one choir-master from each of the three great Levitical branches — Kohath (Heman), Gershon (Asaph), Merari (Ethan) — so that all Levi is represented in the worship of God.

— https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm

---

### v. 48 — "Their fellow Levites were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God."

**Traditional reading:** The Levites not involved in music were assigned to other duties: gatekeepers, caretakers of vessels, slaughtering and preparing sacrifices, etc. Gill enumerates: "some were porters at the gates; others had the care of the vessels; others slew the beasts for sacrifices, flayed them, and cut them up, and brought the pieces to the altar."

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Guzik:** This verse marks the transition from the pedigrees of the three choir-masters to the distinct priestly line of Aaron.

— https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Preacher's Complete Homiletical Commentary:** "Levites employed in door-keeping or attending to priests."

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/phc/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### v. 49 — "But Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place. They presented the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded."

**Traditional reading:** A clear distinction: all Levites served the tabernacle, but only the Aaronic priests offered sacrifices and entered the Most Holy Place. Gill notes this was "according to all that Moses the servant of God commanded" — referring especially to Leviticus 16 (the Day of Atonement). The priests alone "shed the blood of atonement, and burnt incense."

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Coke's Commentary:** "Herein they were typical of him, who, himself both priest and sacrifice, by one oblation of himself once offered, hath obtained eternal redemption for us." This Christological reading is standard across Protestant traditions: the Aaronic priesthood prefigures Christ's once-for-all atonement.

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tcc/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### vv. 50–53 — The descendants of Aaron: Eleazar → Phinehas → Abishua → Bukki → Uzzi → Zerahiah → Meraioth → Amariah → Ahitub → Zadok → Ahimaaz.

**Traditional reading:** This is a partial recapitulation of the high-priestly line from vv. 4–8, stopping at Ahimaaz (who lived in the time of David and Solomon). Ellicott explains that the Chronicler repeats this line as a "new start" before the list of Levitical cities, because the Aaronite priests' cities are to be described first. The list runs "Phinehas his son" rather than "Eleazar begat Phinehas," suggesting a different source document.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

Gill notes the list is "just in the same order as in 1 Chronicles 6:4" through Zadok and Ahimaaz, forming the ancestry of the priests serving in David and Solomon's era.

— https://mail.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_chronicles/6.htm

**The Preacher's Complete Homiletical Commentary** adds: In Eleazar's family the high priesthood remained until the time of Eli (who was descended from Ithamar). It returned to Eleazar's line in Zadok, fulfilling 1 Samuel 2:30.

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/phc/1-chronicles-6.html

---

### v. 54 — "Now these were the territories assigned to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clan for their settlements, because the first lot fell to them."

**Traditional reading:** This introduces the list of Levitical cities (vv. 54–81), which substantially parallels Joshua 21:3–40. Ellicott renders it: "And these were their seats according to their encampments within their border." The clause "for theirs was the lot" (KJV) or "because the first lot fell to them" (BSB) means the Aaronites, being the principal Kohathite branch, received their cities first (Joshua 21:10: "for to them the lot had fallen first").

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

**Benson Commentary:** Calls these "castles" — "not only because walled and well guarded by the country, but because they and their possessions were in a particular manner the care of Divine Providence. As God was their portion, so God was their protector. And a cottage will be a castle to those that abide under the shadow of the Almighty."

— https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/1-chronicles-6.html

**Pulpit Commentary (Homiletics):** The references to priestly cities and provisions are "designed to confirm their claim for reinstatement in their properties on the return from the Captivity." The post-exilic community needed this legal documentation. Also notes the principle that "they who preach the gospel may reasonably expect to live of the gospel" (cf. 1 Corinthians 9:14).

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/1_chronicles/6.htm

---

## Where Protestant Traditions Differ

In the materials retrieved, **no significant denominational disagreements** on this passage emerged. The genealogical and liturgical content of 1 Chronicles 6 is largely treated the same way across Baptist, Reformed, Methodist, Pentecostal, and Lutheran sources. All agree on:

- The historical reliability of the Levitical genealogies
- The Christological typology of the Aaronic priesthood
- The threefold musical leadership of Heman, Asaph, and Ethan/Jeduthun
- The importance of ordered, regulated worship

One subtle difference in emphasis: **Reformed** sources (like Ligonier) tend to emphasize that the tabernacle and temple were "never meant to be permanent" — they prefigured Christ, in whom all believers become priests. **Pentecostal/charismatic** sources (like Enduring Word) may place more emphasis on the prophetic dimension of music ministry (1 Chronicles 25:1 notes that Heman's sons "prophesied" with music). However, these differences are of emphasis rather than interpretive conflict on this specific passage.

— https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/numbering-the-levites
— https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm (Guzik)

---

## Other Views

### Modern Scholarship / Text-Critical Notes

**Ellicott** (representing the older critical tradition still used broadly) notes several textual issues: the "Vashni" corruption in v. 28; the variant name-forms between the fragmentary genealogy (vv. 22–28) and the continuous one (vv. 33–38) — e.g., Zophai/Zuph, Nahath/Toah, Eliab/Eliel, Uriel/Zephaniah, Shaul/Joel; and the likely omission of "Samuel his son" at the end of v. 27. He concludes the Chronicler used multiple independent genealogical fragments.

— https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/1_chronicles/6.htm

### Catholic and Orthodox Readings

No distinct Catholic or Orthodox commentary on this specific passage was retrievable from the permitted sites (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org) within the search limits. The Catholic tradition generally treats these genealogies as part of the inspired historical record and reads the Aaronic priesthood typologically in relation to the priesthood of Christ and, in a derived sense, the ministerial priesthood of the New Covenant. The Orthodox tradition similarly reads the passage within the context of the Church's liturgical life, seeing David's organization of temple musicians as a foreshadowing of ordered Christian worship.

---

## Summary of Key Themes

1. **Samuel's Levitical lineage** (v. 28 → v. 33): Heman, David's chief musician, was Samuel's grandson — confirming that the prophet belonged to the tribe of Levi through Kohath.
2. **Ordered worship** (vv. 31–32): David instituted the musical ministry after the Ark found its resting place, and this order continued until — and within — Solomon's Temple.
3. **The three choirs** (vv. 33–47): Heman (centre, Kohathite), Asaph (right, Gershonite), Ethan/Jeduthun (left, Merarite) — all three branches of Levi represented.
4. **Distinction of roles** (vv. 48–49): All Levites served, but only Aaron's sons offered sacrifice and entered the Most Holy Place — a distinction pointing typologically to Christ.
5. **Priestly inheritance** (v. 54): The Aaronites received their cities first by lot, and God Himself was their ultimate portion and protector.
